title: Sphere Volume Derivative Visualization
full_prompt: Write a ManimGL script that visualizes the derivative of a sphere's volume with respect to its radius, building upon a 2D circle area derivative visualization. First, create a base class `ShowCircleAreaDerivative` inheriting from `InteractiveScene`. In this class, render a 2D circle of radius $r=2$ labeled 'A' with a radial line and 'r' label. Use a `ValueTracker` for $dr$ (initially 0.5) to dynamically draw an outer annulus representing $dA$ with thickness $dr$. Animate $dr$ shrinking from 0.5 to 0, then to 0.5, and then to 0.1. Second, create a subclass `ShowSphereVolumeDerivative` that transitions this concept to 3D. Set the floor plane to 'xz' and reorient the camera frame. Render a 3D inner sphere of radius $r=3$ (colored teal with a white `SurfaceMesh` overlay) and apply a clipping plane. Create a dynamically redrawn outer sphere of radius $r + dr$ (colored semi-transparent red) representing the volume increment $dV$. Animate the camera reorienting while opening up the clipping plane, then animate the outer sphere expanding as $dr$ goes to 0.5, shrinking to 0.1, and finally smoothly shrinking to 0.0 while fading out the labels.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Using Manim Community (CE) syntax for camera control instead of ManimGL's self.frame.reorient
common_failure_modes.note: The script relies heavily on ManimGL's InteractiveScene camera frame manipulation.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Missing SurfaceMesh or set_clip_plane support in non-GL environments
common_failure_modes.note: SurfaceMesh and set_clip_plane are specific to ManimGL/modern OpenGL renderers and will fail in standard CE.
Failing to set the floor plane to 'xz' will cause the 3D sphere and 2D circle overlays to align incorrectly.
